Dear Colleague,

Reason for referral: Evaluation of perioperative cardiac risk before planned non-cardiac surgery.

Henry Lewis is a 46-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and primary hypothyroidism who is scheduled for elective hernia repair. He reports no chest discomfort, shortness of breath, or fainting with routine activity.

Please assess his perioperative cardiac risk before this planned non-cardiac surgery and advise the surgical team on preparation for the procedure.

Thank you for seeing this patient.

Dr. Samuel Reed
Atlas Medical Group

The acute illness was characterized by upper abdominal pain, nausea, and inability to tolerate his usual meals. The overall clinical assessment favored inflammation of the pancreas related to gallstone disease. He required inpatient supportive care, observation, and evaluation by the treating teams. There was no indication in the documented course of a separate acute condition requiring treatment. The admission goals were to control pain and nausea, provide hydration, monitor recovery and oral intake, assess the biliary cause, and determine the safest timing for definitive treatment. His established chronic conditions were considered throughout the stay, with attention to maintaining continuity of care and avoiding unnecessary interruption of his routine outpatient plan.
